brief:
An ultra-Orthodox rabbi's comments questioning Zionism have intensified tensions during Israel's election campaign, according to Al Jazeera English. Rabbi Dov Lando's remarks have exposed deep rifts over core ideological questions and the role of ultra-Orthodox parties in Israeli politics, particularly those allied with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The controversy centres on disputes between ultra-Orthodox communities and mainstream Israeli society over conscription and the definition of Jewish statehood. Ultra-Orthodox parties have long sought exemptions from military service for their members, a position that has fueled ongoing political friction as Netanyahu relies on their coalition support.
dek: Rabbi Dov Lando's comments expose tensions over Zionism, conscription and Netanyahu's ultra-Orthodox allies.
title: Ultra-Orthodox rabbi's anti-Zionist remarks ignite Israeli election dispute
